name: Secondary Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Childhood Associated with a Connective Tissue Disease
aliases: Childhood Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Pediatric Connective Tissue Disease-Associated ILD Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Clinical or serological evidence of an underlying connective tissue disease (e.g., juvenile dermatomyositis, systemic lupus erythematosus, juvenile systemic sclerosis)
Radiological and/or histopathological evidence of interstitial lung disease consistent with CTD-associated patterns
Exclusion of other causes of interstitial lung disease such as infection, environmental exposures, or primary pulmonary disorders
Restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing with reduced diffusion capacity
Presence of disease-specific autoantibodies (e.g., anti-RNP, anti-Jo-1, anti-Scl-70)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical or serological evidence of connective tissue disease plus radiological or histopathological confirmation of interstitial lung disease, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including rheumatology, pulmonology, and radiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic auscultatory finding in interstitial lung disease
Indicative of chronic hypoxia and lung fibrosis
Common in connective tissue diseases associated with ILD

common.notes: Early symptom reflecting impaired gas exchange
searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.notes: Persistent dry cough due to lung fibrosis
Joint involvement related to underlying connective tissue disease
Cutaneous manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus
Seen in juvenile dermatomyositis or polymyositis

occasional.notes: Skin thickening seen in systemic sclerosis

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic lung disease and vascular involvement
Rare, may indicate severe lung injury or vasculitis
Inflammation of pericardium in connective tissue disease

laboratory: Positive autoimmune serologies (ANA, anti-RNP, anti-Jo-1, anti-Scl-70)
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, reticulation, and honeycombing
Reduced lung volumes on chest radiograph
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; familial clustering rare
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive defect and reduced diffusion capacity
Histopathology demonstrating nonspecific interstitial pneumonia or usual interstitial pneumonia patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of connective tissue disease features or autoantibodies
Rapid onset with systemic signs of infection

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
references: Meyer KC et al. Interstitial Lung Disease in Children with Connective Tissue Disease. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2022;57(3):555-567.
Orphanet Report: Secondary Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Childhood Associated with Connective Tissue Disease, ORPHA:264704.
American Thoracic Society Guidelines for Pediatric Interstitial Lung Disease, 2021.
